season.evidence: Our only route; 600+ logged successful ascents peak Jul-Sep (Jun 38, Oct 58). Searches (Outdoor Project, Mountaineers, WTA, trail guides) put Gothic Basin snow-free from late Jul to mid Oct with axe/crampons advised into late Aug; Jun/early Jul need axe, Nov has fresh snow. Stored Jul-Sep kept.

track.why: Only route we hold on the peak. Logged Standard Route, 12 Aug 2021, summited; track starts 40 m from our Barlow Pass pin, ends 42 m from it, passes 5 m from our summit pin, and follows the Gothic Basin / Foggy Lake line (about 4,500 ft gain).

otherTracksConsidered.why: Also Standard Route, Sep 2024, in season, but start 87 m / loop 119 m; 1730487 is cleaner
Jul 2023 logged South Gully; start 140 m off our pin; same peak line but the gully is not recommended by our text

facts.text: In early July the trail from about 4,000 ft is snow-covered, the basin lakes are still frozen, and soft snow persists up to the notch below the summit gully.
Mid-July: a snow patch sits just below the notch gully but is soft enough to cross without an axe
Keep to the left-hand ledges all the way up; the central gully to the notch is not the line.
Barlow Pass lot holds about 30 cars and fills before 6:30 am on a late-July Saturday; roadside spots just outside work, and the Forest Pass is needed inside the lot.
Take the first signed right off the old road for Gothic Basin; the later junction leads to a brushed-over trail.
Water is plentiful at the stream crossings and Foggy Lake in July, so carry little from the trailhead.
In mid-August a firm perennial snowfield below the ridge is easiest to skirt via its upper moat, not traverse in boots
Blue flags and cairns mark the climbers path along the north side of Foggy Lake and up the talus in August.

notes: Single route on peak; track assignment rests on the one-route rule plus the route name and geometry. No trailhead/summit pin changes: all tracks start within 150 m of our pin.
